questions.subject: STATISTICS

Response bias because answers may be untruthful.

Elimination of all confounding variables.
Representativeness of the tank population.
Causal claims about diet effects on growth.

questions.explanation: Random assignment supports causal conclusions about treatment effects. Generalization requires random sampling from a larger population.

options.text: To provide a baseline for comparison.

To eliminate random variation.

A control variable because it is held constant.

No blinding because diets look different.
Double-blinding because both parties are unaware.

questions.explanation: When both subjects and researchers are unaware of treatment assignment, the study is double-blind. Blinding reduces bias in measurement and response.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: Why is it important to repeat an experiment on many fish rather than one?

questions.explanation: Replication helps distinguish treatment effects from random variation. A single observation cannot separate signal from noise.

questions.stem: Why is convenience sampling risky for inference?

questions.stem: How do researchers account for placebo effects in experiments?

questions.stem: Why does blinding reduce bias in experiments?
